annotations.description:
Unstructured key value map that may be set by external tools to store and arbitrary metadata. They are not queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects.

Cloud Run API v2 does not support annotations with 'run.googleapis.com', 'cloud.googleapis.com', 'serving.knative.dev', or 'autoscaling.knative.dev' namespaces, and they will be rejected on new resources.
All system annotations in v1 now have a corresponding field in v2 Job.

This field follows Kubernetes annotations' namespacing, limits, and rules.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: No direct security risk as it stores metadata and does not influence security behavior.

client.description: Arbitrary identifier for the API client.
client.rationale: No direct security risk as it is an identifier for the client

client_version.description: Arbitrary version identifier for the API client.
client_version.rationale: No direct security risk as it only tracks version information and does not affect security controls.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

deletion_protection.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the job. Defaults to true.
When a'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the job,
the command will fail if this field is not set to false in Terraform state.
When the field is set to true or unset in Terraform state, a 'terraform apply'
or 'terraform destroy' that would delete the job will fail.
When the field is set to false, deleting the job is allowed.
deletion_protection.rationale: Prevents accidental deletion of Cloud Run Jobs by enforcing deletion protection.

labels.description:
Unstructured key value map that can be used to organize and categorize objects. User-provided labels are shared with Google's billing system, so they can be used to filter, or break down billing charges by team, component,
environment, state, etc. For more information, visit https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-labels or https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/labels.

Cloud Run API v2 does not support labels with 'run.googleapis.com', 'cloud.googleapis.com', 'serving.knative.dev', or 'autoscaling.knative.dev' namespaces, and they will be rejected.
All system labels in v1 now have a corresponding field in v2 Job.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: No direct security risk as it only provides organizational metadata

launch_stage.description:
The launch stage as defined by [Google Cloud Platform Launch Stages](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages). Cloud Run supports ALPHA, BETA, and GA.
If no value is specified, GA is assumed. Set the launch stage to a preview stage on input to allow use of preview features in that stage. On read (or output), describes whether the resource uses preview features.

For example, if ALPHA is provided as input, but only BETA and GA-level features are used, this field will be BETA on output. Possible values: ["UNIMPLEMENTED", "PRELAUNCH", "EARLY_ACCESS", "ALPHA", "BETA", "GA", "DEPRECATED"]
launch_stage.rationale: Selects the API launch stage (ALPHA/BETA/GA) of features used by the resource. This governs feature maturity/stability, not a security control — restricting it improves reliability, not the security posture of the resource — and the same field is (correctly) marked false on the worker pool.

location.description: The location of the cloud run job
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.rationale: This field does not introduce direct security risk as it only defines an identifier.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: No direct security risk as it specifies project context

binary_authorization.description: Settings for the Binary Authorization feature.

binary_authorization.breakglass_justific.description: If present, indicates to use Breakglass using this justification. If useDefault is False, then it must be empty. For more information on breakglass, see https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/using-breakglass
binary_authorization.breakglass_justific.rationale: No direct security risk as it only provides a justification string for an override mechanism.

binary_authorization.policy.description: The path to a binary authorization policy. Format: projects/{project}/platforms/cloudRun/{policy-name}
binary_authorization.policy.rationale: No direct security risk as it only references a policy resource or the location path

binary_authorization.use_default.description: If True, indicates to use the default project's binary authorization policy. If False, binary authorization will be disabled.
binary_authorization.use_default.rationale: Ensures only trusted and verified container images are deployed by enforcing Binary Authorization.

template.description: The template used to create executions for this Job.

template.annotations.description:
Unstructured key value map that may be set by external tools to store and arbitrary metadata. They are not queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects.

Cloud Run API v2 does not support annotations with 'run.googleapis.com', 'cloud.googleapis.com', 'serving.knative.dev', or 'autoscaling.knative.dev' namespaces, and they will be rejected.
All system annotations in v1 now have a corresponding field in v2 ExecutionTemplate.

This field follows Kubernetes annotations' namespacing, limits, and rules.
template.annotations.rationale: No direct security risk as it only stores arbitrary metadata and does not influence security boundaries

template.labels.description:
Unstructured key value map that can be used to organize and categorize objects. User-provided labels are shared with Google's billing system, so they can be used to filter,
or break down billing charges by team, component, environment, state, etc. For more information, visit https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-labels or
https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/labels.

Cloud Run API v2 does not support labels with 'run.googleapis.com', 'cloud.googleapis.com', 'serving.knative.dev', or 'autoscaling.knative.dev' namespaces, and they will be rejected.
All system labels in v1 now have a corresponding field in v2 ExecutionTemplate.
template.labels.rationale: No direct security risk as it only defines metadata for organization

template.parallelism.description: Specifies the maximum desired number of tasks the execution should run at given time. Must be <= taskCount. When the job is run, if this field is 0 or unset, the maximum possible value will be used for that execution. The actual number of tasks running in steady state will be less than this number when there are fewer tasks waiting to be completed remaining, i.e. when the work left to do is less than max parallelism.
template.parallelism.rationale: No direct security risk as it only controls task concurrency

template.task_count.description: Specifies the desired number of tasks the execution should run. Setting to 1 means that parallelism is limited to 1 and the success of that task signals the success of the execution. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/jobs-run-to-completion/
template.task_count.rationale: No direct security risk as it only defines workload scaling

template.template.description: Describes the task(s) that will be created when executing an execution

template.template.encryption_key.description: A reference to a customer managed encryption key (CMEK) to use to encrypt this container image. For more information, go to https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/using-cmek
template.template.encryption_key.rationale: Enforces use of approved customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) from authorized KMS key rings and regions to ensure controlled data encryption.

template.template.execution_environment.description: The execution environment being used to host this Task. Possible values: ["EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT_GEN1", "EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT_GEN2"]
template.template.execution_environment.rationale: No direct security risk as it selects the runtime environment version without directly affecting security controls.

template.template.gpu_zonal_redundancy_d.description: True if GPU zonal redundancy is disabled on this execution.
template.template.gpu_zonal_redundancy_d.rationale: No direct security risk as it controls availability characteristics and does not affect security mechanisms.

template.template.max_retries.description: Number of retries allowed per Task, before marking this Task failed. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 0.
template.template.max_retries.rationale: Sets how many times a failed task is retried. This is an operational reliability/cost setting; bounding it does not protect data or access. It is the team's workload-management choice, consistent with how CPU/memory limits are treated as non-security here.

template.template.service_account.description: Email address of the IAM service account associated with the Task of a Job. The service account represents the identity of the running task, and determines what permissions the task has. If not provided, the task will use the project's default service account.
template.template.service_account.rationale: Prevents privilege escalation risks by blocking default service accounts and enforcing least-privileged dedicated identities for Cloud Run Jobs.

template.template.timeout.description:
Max allowed time duration the Task may be active before the system will actively try to mark it failed and kill associated containers. This applies per attempt of a task, meaning each retry can run for the full timeout.

A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.5s".
template.template.timeout.rationale: No direct security risk as it only defines execution duration limits

template.template.containers.description: Holds the single container that defines the unit of execution for this task.

template.template.containers.args.description: Arguments to the entrypoint. The docker image's CMD is used if this is not provided. Variable references are not supported in Cloud Run.
template.template.containers.args.rationale: No direct security risk as it provides runtime arguments

template.template.containers.command.description: Entrypoint array. Not executed within a shell. The docker image's ENTRYPOINT is used if this is not provided. Variable references $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the container's environment. If a variable cannot be resolved, the reference in the input string will be unchanged. The $(VAR_NAME) syntax can be escaped with a double $$, ie: $$(VAR_NAME). Escaped references will never be expanded, regardless of whether the variable exists or not. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/inject-data-application/define-command-argument-container/#running-a-command-in-a-shell
template.template.containers.command.rationale: No direct security risk as it defines runtime behavior but does not inherently introduce security control weaknesses

template.template.containers.depends_on.description: Names of the containers that must start before this container.
template.template.containers.depends_on.rationale: No direct security risk as it controls startup order.

template.template.containers.image.description: URL of the Container image in Google Container Registry or Google Artifact Registry. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images
template.template.containers.image.rationale: Enforces use of approved container registries like Artifact Registry by blocking images from public registries to reduce supply chain risk.

template.template.containers.name.description: Name of the container specified as a DNS_LABEL.

template.template.containers.working_dir.description: Container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default will be used, which might be configured in the container image.
template.template.containers.working_dir.rationale: No direct security risk as it defines runtime directory context.

template.template.containers.env.description: List of environment variables to set in the container.

template.template.containers.env.name.description: Name of the environment variable. Must be a C_IDENTIFIER, and mnay not exceed 32768 characters.

template.template.containers.env.value.description: Literal value of the environment variable. Defaults to "" and the maximum allowed length is 32768 characters. Variable references are not supported in Cloud Run.

template.template.containers.env.value_s.description: Source for the environment variable's value.
Selects a secret and a specific version from Cloud Secret Manager.
The name of the secret in Cloud Secret Manager. Format: {secretName} if the secret is in the same project. projects/{project}/secrets/{secretName} if the secret is in a different project.
The Cloud Secret Manager secret version. Can be 'latest' for the latest value or an integer for a specific version.

template.template.containers.ports.description:
List of ports to expose from the container. Only a single port can be specified. The specified ports must be listening on all interfaces (0.0.0.0) within the container to be accessible.

If omitted, a port number will be chosen and passed to the container through the PORT environment variable for the container to listen on

template.template.containers.ports.conta.description: Port number the container listens on. This must be a valid TCP port number, 0 < containerPort < 65536.
template.template.containers.ports.conta.rationale: defines the port number used by the container and does not introduce any direct security implications.

template.template.containers.ports.name.description: If specified, used to specify which protocol to use. Allowed values are "http1" and "h2c".

template.template.containers.resources.description: Compute Resource requirements by this container. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#resources

template.template.containers.resources.l.description: Only memory, CPU, and nvidia.com/gpu are supported. Use key 'cpu' for CPU limit, 'memory' for memory limit, 'nvidia.com/gpu' for gpu limit. Note: The only supported values for CPU are '1', '2', '4', '6', and '8'. Setting 4 CPU requires at least 2Gi of memory, setting 6 or more CPU requires at least 4Gi of memory. The values of the map is string form of the 'quantity' k8s type: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go
template.template.containers.resources.l.rationale: This only specifies upper limits for CPU, memory, or GPU usage and is related to performance

template.template.containers.startup_pro.description:
Startup probe of application within the container.
All other probes are disabled if a startup probe is provided, until it
succeeds. Container will not be added to service endpoints if the probe fails.

Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after
having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.
template.template.containers.startup_pro.rationale: This defines retry behavior for probes and does not introduce any security risk

template.template.containers.startup_pro.description:
Number of seconds after the container has started before the probe is
initiated.
Defaults to 0 seconds. Minimum value is 0. Maximum value is 240.
template.template.containers.startup_pro.rationale: This defines timing behavior for health checks and has no impact on security controls.

template.template.containers.startup_pro.description:
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe.
Default to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1. Maximum value is 240.
template.template.containers.startup_pro.rationale: This controls how frequently probes run and is operational rather than security-related.

template.template.containers.startup_pro.description:
Number of seconds after which the probe times out.
Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1. Maximum value is 3600.
Must be smaller than periodSeconds.
template.template.containers.startup_pro.rationale: This specifies probe timeout settings and does not influence security.

template.template.containers.startup_pro.description: GRPC specifies an action involving a GRPC port.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.

The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest
(see https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/health-checking.md).
If this is not specified, the default behavior is defined by gRPC.
template.template.containers.startup_pro.rationale: This defines the service name for health checks

template.template.containers.startup_pro.description: HttpGet specifies the http request to perform.
Path to access on the HTTP server. If set, it should not be empty string.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.
Custom headers to set in the request. HTTP allows repeated headers.
TcpSocket specifies an action involving a TCP port.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.

template.template.containers.volume_moun.description: Volume to mount into the container's filesystem.

Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must not contain ':'. For Cloud SQL volumes, it can be left empty, or must otherwise be /cloudsql. All instances defined in the Volume will be available as /cloudsql/[instance]. For more information on Cloud SQL volumes, visit https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-run
template.template.containers.volume_moun.rationale: This specifies where the volume is mounted inside the container

template.template.containers.volume_moun.description: This must match the Name of a Volume.
Path within the volume from which the container's volume should be mounted.

template.template.node_selector.description: Node Selector describes the hardware requirements of the resources.

template.template.node_selector.accelera.description: The GPU to attach to an instance. See https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/jobs/gpu for configuring GPU.
template.template.node_selector.accelera.rationale: his specifies GPU usage and does not need restriction as it is not security-sensitive.

template.template.volumes.description: A list of Volumes to make available to containers.

template.template.volumes.cloud_sql_inst.description: For Cloud SQL volumes, contains the specific instances that should be mounted. Visit https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-run for more information on how to connect Cloud SQL and Cloud Run.

The Cloud SQL instance connection names, as can be found in https://console.cloud.google.com/sql/instances. Visit https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-run for more information on how to connect Cloud SQL and Cloud Run. Format: {project}:{location}:{instance}
template.template.volumes.cloud_sql_inst.rationale: This lists database instances and does not need security enforcement

template.template.volumes.empty_dir.description: Ephemeral storage used as a shared volume.

template.template.volumes.empty_dir.medi.description: The different types of medium supported for EmptyDir. Default value: "MEMORY" Possible values: ["MEMORY", "DISK"]
template.template.volumes.empty_dir.medi.rationale: This defines storage type and does not need security controls

template.template.volumes.empty_dir.size.description: Limit on the storage usable by this EmptyDir volume. The size limit is also applicable for memory medium. The maximum usage on memory medium EmptyDir would be the minimum value between the SizeLimit specified here and the sum of memory limits of all containers in a pod. This field's values are of the 'Quantity' k8s type: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/common-definitions/quantity/. The default is nil which means that the limit is undefined. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#emptydir.
template.template.volumes.empty_dir.size.rationale: This sets storage limits and is not related to security enforcment

template.template.volumes.gcs.description: Cloud Storage bucket mounted as a volume using GCSFuse.

template.template.volumes.gcs.bucket.description: Name of the cloud storage bucket to back the volume. The resource service account must have permission to access the bucket.
template.template.volumes.gcs.bucket.rationale: This specifies a bucket name and does not require policies here.

template.template.volumes.gcs.mount_opti.description:
A list of flags to pass to the gcsfuse command for configuring this volume.
Flags should be passed without leading dashes.
template.template.volumes.gcs.mount_opti.rationale: This defines mount behavior and does not need policy as it does not affect access control.

template.template.volumes.gcs.read_only.description: If true, mount this volume as read-only in all mounts. If false, mount this volume as read-write.

template.template.volumes.nfs.description: NFS share mounted as a volume.

template.template.volumes.nfs.path.description: Path that is exported by the NFS server.

template.template.volumes.nfs.read_only.description: If true, mount this volume as read-only in all mounts.

template.template.volumes.nfs.server.description: Hostname or IP address of the NFS server.
template.template.volumes.nfs.server.rationale: This specifies the server endpoint and does not require policy since network-level controls handle security.

template.template.volumes.secret.description: Secret represents a secret that should populate this volume. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes#secret

template.template.volumes.secret.default.description: Integer representation of mode bits to use on created files by default. Must be a value between 0000 and 0777 (octal), defaulting to 0444. Directories within the path are not affected by this setting.
template.template.volumes.secret.default.rationale: This defines file permission defaults but does not need to be enforced with security policies.

template.template.volumes.secret.secret.description: The name of the secret in Cloud Secret Manager. Format: {secret} if the secret is in the same project. projects/{project}/secrets/{secret} if the secret is in a different project.

template.template.volumes.secret.items.description: If unspecified, the volume will expose a file whose name is the secret, relative to VolumeMount.mount_path. If specified, the key will be used as the version to fetch from Cloud Secret Manager and the path will be the name of the file exposed in the volume. When items are defined, they must specify a path and a version.

template.template.volumes.secret.items.m.description: Integer octal mode bits to use on this file, must be a value between 01 and 0777 (octal). If 0 or not set, the Volume's default mode will be used.
template.template.volumes.secret.items.m.rationale: This defines permissions and does not require any security policy.

template.template.volumes.secret.items.p.description: The relative path of the secret in the container.

template.template.volumes.secret.items.v.description: The Cloud Secret Manager secret version. Can be 'latest' for the latest value or an integer for a specific version

template.template.vpc_access.description: VPC Access configuration to use for this Task. For more information, visit https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/connecting-vpc.

template.template.vpc_access.connector.description: VPC Access connector name. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/connectors/{connector}, where {project} can be project id or number.
template.template.vpc_access.connector.rationale: This specifies the connector to use and does not require restriction because security policies are enforced at the network configuration level.

template.template.vpc_access.egress.description: Traffic VPC egress settings. Possible values: ["ALL_TRAFFIC", "PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY"]
template.template.vpc_access.egress.rationale: Reduces the risk of data being leaked outside the network by preventing Cloud Run Jobs from sending traffic to unrestricted external destinations.

template.template.vpc_access.network_int.description: Direct VPC egress settings. Currently only single network interface is supported.

The VPC network that the Cloud Run resource will be able to send traffic to. At least one of network or subnetwork must be specified. If both
network and subnetwork are specified, the given VPC subnetwork must belong to the given VPC network. If network is not specified, it will be
looked up from the subnetwork.
template.template.vpc_access.network_int.rationale: This specifies the network and does not need restriction.

template.template.vpc_access.network_int.description:
The VPC subnetwork that the Cloud Run resource will get IPs from. At least one of network or subnetwork must be specified. If both
network and subnetwork are specified, the given VPC subnetwork must belong to the given VPC network. If subnetwork is not specified, the
subnetwork with the same name with the network will be used.
template.template.vpc_access.network_int.rationale: This defines subnetwork configuration and does not require restriction as it does not enforce security policies.

template.template.vpc_access.network_int.description: Network tags applied to this Cloud Run job.
template.template.vpc_access.network_int.rationale: This defines network tags and does not need restriction because they do not directly control access.
